findings.evidence: naming-conventions.md: "Coercions are named after the underlying function". mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Units/Defs.lean:280 `val_inv_eq_inv_val`, Units/Basic.lean:123 `val_inv_inj`; code/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/JordanChevalley/Multiplicative.lean:124,145 use `Units.val_pow_eq_pow_val`, `Units.val_mul`. Closest adjoin-membership precedent: mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Subalgebra/Lattice.lean:805 `Algebra.self_mem_adjoin_singleton`.
findings.fix: Rename to `val_inv_mem_adjoin` (or `val_inv_mem_adjoin_singleton`, matching `Algebra.self_mem_adjoin_singleton`), and update the use in `JordanChevalley/Multiplicative.lean:108` and the module doc line 19.
findings.issue: `Units.coe_inv_mem_adjoin` names the `Aˣ → A` coercion `coe_`, but the underlying function is `Units.val` and the modern Units API spells it `val_` — this PR's own proofs use `Units.val_mul` and `Units.val_pow_eq_pow_val` for the same coercion, so a reader grepping `Units.val_inv…` will not find this lemma.

findings.evidence: In Mathlib, ~20 files about units are named `Units.lean` (e.g. `Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Units.lean`, `Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Ring/Units.lean`), while the only `Unit.lean` is `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Unit.lean` (about the `Unit` type). The repo follows this: `code/TauCeti/Algebra/Order/Ring/Units.lean`.
findings.fix: Rename the module to `TauCeti/RingTheory/Adjoin/Units.lean` and update the import in `JordanChevalley/Multiplicative.lean:8`.
findings.issue: The module is named `Unit.lean` (singular), which by Mathlib convention denotes the `Unit` type, not `Units`; the file is entirely about `Aˣ`.

summary: Names in the semisimple-point and GL closure API follow Mathlib precedent, no notation is introduced, and the prior round's namespace/module-name findings are fixed. Two residual naming items remain in the new `RingTheory/Adjoin` module: the `coe_` spelling of the `Units.val` coercion and the singular `Unit.lean` module name.
